questions.question: The historical Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between** __Delhi and Amritsar. __**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sher-Shah Suri Marg is a historical road that was built during the reign of Sher Shah Suri in the 16th century.**
 
• It was built to connect the Mughal Empire's capital Delhi with the province of Punjab. The road was later extended to the Afghan border during the British era.
 
• The road is also known as the Grand Trunk Road and is one of the oldest and longest roads in South Asia. It covers a distance of over 2,500 km and passes through several major cities like Delhi, Amritsar, Lahore, and Kolkata.
 
• The road played a significant role in the trade and commerce of the Mughal Empire and later the British Raj. It was also an important route for the movement of troops during wars and conflicts.
 
• The road has undergone several renovations and upgrades over the years, but it still retains its historical significance and attracts tourists from all over the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sher Shah Suri Marg

 
 
• National Highway No.1 is known as Sher Shah Suri Marg
 
• It connects Delhi To Amritsar via Ambala and Jalandhar
 
• Previously it was known as Grand Trunk Road (GT Road)
 
• It was built by Sher Shah Suri in the 16th century
 
 
 
• Sher Shah Suri
 
 
• Founder of the Suri Dynasty in India
 
• Grand Trunk Road (GT Road)
 
• The oldest and longest road in Asia
 
• It runs roughly 2400km from Teknaf, Bangladesh to Kabul, Afghanistan.

questions.question: Udaipur was founded by ______ after the fall of Chittor to Akbar in 1568.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Udai Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rana Udai Singh**

 
 
• Udaipur was founded by Maharana Udai Singh after the fall of Chittor to Akbar in **1568**.
 
• Rana Udai Singh was the ruler of the kingdom of Mewar in present-day** Rajasthan,** India.
 
• When the Mughal emperor Akbar seized Chittor, which was then the **capital of Mewar**, Udai Singh moved his capital to a more secure location.
 
• As per the advice of a hermit, he chose the area around **Lake Pichola** for his new capital, which was named after him as Udaipur.
 
• Unlike most other Rajput kingdoms, Mewar continued to resist the Mughals, under the leadership of several generations of **Sisodia Rajputs**.
 
• Rana Udai Singh and his successors, notably **Maharana Pratap Singh**, are remembered as national heroes in India for their resistance to the Mughals, especially Akbar.
 
• The city of Udaipur is celebrated for its lake-studded, romantic setting and sweeping architectural grandeur, including magnificent palaces such as the **City Palace, Lake Palace, and Jag Mandi**r.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Name
 Information
 
 
 
 

 **Man Singh**
 Man Singh (1540-1614) was the Rajput Raja of Amer (Jaipur), a state in Rajasthan, India. He was a trusted general in the court of the Mughal emperor Akbar, who included him among his 'navaratnas', or nine gems. Man Singh helped Akbar consolidate his empire through his military and diplomatic skills.
 
 

 **Raja Bharmal**
 Raja Bharmal of Amber (also in Rajasthan) was the first Rajput ruler to marry his daughter, Harkha Bai (later known as Jodha Bai or Mariam-uz-Zamani), to a Mughal - Emperor Akbar. This alliance was a fundamental turning point which began a tradition of Rajput-Mughal political marriages, aiding the stabilization of relations between the two powers.
 
 

 **Sawai Jai Singh**
 Sawai Jai Singh II (1688-1743) was the founder of Jaipur city, the capital of Rajasthan. An esteemed ruler of the Kachwaha clan of Rajputs, he was also an avid astronomer and built several observatories known as 'Jantar Mantars' in different cities of India. During his reign, architecture, education, and astronomy flourished, leading to significant advancements. Jai Singh's most significant achievement was the construction of Jaipur, which was designed according to the principles of Vastu Shastra and Shilpa Shastra, becoming one of the earliest examples of a planned city in India.

questions.question: Sultan Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraja III in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1192.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sultan Muhammad Ghori** defeated **Prithviraja III **in the year **1192** in the **Second Battle of Tarain**.
 
• **Prithviraja III** was the last Hindu king of the **Chauhan dynasty of Delhi.**
 
• The battle between Sultan Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraja III was known as the **Second Battle of Tarain.**
 
• The defeat of Prithviraja III marked the beginning of **Muslim rule in Northern India.**
 
• Sultan Muhammad Ghori was a **Persian ruler **who founded the **Ghurid dynasty** in **Afghanistan and North India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The year 1191 is significant in Indian history as it marks the **First Battle of Tarain** in which **Prithviraja III defeated Sultan Muhammad Ghori.**
 
• The **kingdom of Sapadalaksha** was ruled by Prithviraja III who had his capital at** Ajmer** in modern-day Rajasthan. 
 
• From **1173 to 1206,** Muhammad Ghori, a member of the Ghurid dynasty based in what is now central **Afghanistan,** was in charge.
 
• Up until Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad's passing in** 1203**, Muhammad of Ghor and his older brother Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad held dynastic rule.

questions.question: When was the Battle of Tukaroi fought where Akbar defeated Sultanate of Bengal and Bihar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1575.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The Battle of Tukaroi **was fought on **March 3, 1575,** between the Mughal Empire led by** Akbar and** the Sultanate of Bengal and Bihar led by** Daud Khan Karrani.**
 
• It was a significant battle in the history of medieval India, as it marked the beginning of the end of the** Karrani dynasty's rule in Bengal and Bihar.**
 
• Akbar's victory in the Battle of Tukaroi was due to his **superior military tactics and the effective use of firearms**, which gave the Mughals an edge over their opponents.
 
• **The battle was also significant because it paved the way for Akbar's expansion **of the Mughal Empire in the east, eventually leading to the annexation of Bengal and Bihar.

• Mathura and Gandhara's school of art flourished during his reign.

questions.question: Who among the following took the title of ‘Ghazi’ after defeating Rana Sanga in the Battle of Khanwa in 1527?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Babur of the Mughal Empire** and** Rajput King Rana Sanga of Mewar** fought each other in** Khanwa, 60 kilometers west of Agra.**
 
• The event to gain control of** Northern India **took place on **March 16, 1527. **
 
• **Sangram Singh** was regarded as one of** India's greatest historical figures.**
 
• Rana Sanga aspired to be the** supreme leader** of India.
 
• The** Khanwa battle **was won by **Babur.**
 
• After the** Battle of Khanwa,** Babur held the title of **Ghazi (17th March 1527).**

questions.question: Which state of India was ruled by the Ningthouja dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Manipur.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The **descendants of Manipur's kings** make up the **Ningthouja dynasty**, commonly known as the** Mangang dynasty.**
 
• Ningthouja literally translates to **"King's Progeny."**
 
• There are **125 extended families** living there. In **33 CE, King Nongda Lairen Pakhangba** is said to have** founded** it.
 
• Emperor Nongta Lailen Pakhangpa whose identity is often mingled with that of** Pakhangpa, **the serpentine dragon god of Meitei mythology and religion.
 
• The **Ningthouja dynast**y was one of the **three most powerful **dynasties, the others being** Luwang dynasty and Khuman dynasty.**
 
• By the beginning of the** 1st millennium CE**, the Ningthouja Dynasty began to emerge in **Imphal River valley**, overrunning the territory of the** Khaba clan**. They established** Kangla** as their **seat of power.**

questions.question: Who built an elegant two-storey 'ship palace' between two reservoirs named Jahaz Mahal?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sultan Ghiyasuddin Khilji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jahaz Mahal**, also known as the "Ship Palace," is a remarkable architectural structure located in **Mandu, Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• It was constructed during the reign of **Sultan Ghiyasuddin Khilji**, one of the rulers of the **Malwa Sultanate.**
 
• The palace was built between two artificial reservoirs, namely the **Kapur Talao** and **Munja Talao**, creating the illusion of a ship floating on water.
 
• **Sultan Ghiyasuddin Khilji** was known for his love of art, architecture, and luxurious lifestyle, which is reflected in the design of Jahaz Mahal.
 
• The primary purpose of the palace was to accommodate the royal harem, which included thousands of women, and provide a serene and picturesque environment for leisure and entertainment.
 
• The architectural style of Jahaz Mahal showcases the blending of **Islamic** and **local Indian designs,** demonstrating the cultural synthesis of the period.
 
• The palace features intricate carvings, expansive halls, and terraces, along with water channels that enhanced its aesthetic appeal.
 
• Jahaz Mahal is a popular tourist destination and an important historical site that reflects the grandeur of the **Malwa Sultanate.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sultan Muhammad Bin Tughlaq**__

 __
 
• **Sultan Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** was the ruler of the **Tughlaq dynasty** in Delhi and is known for his ambitious but often impractical projects.
 
• He shifted the capital from Delhi to **Daulatabad** and introduced token currency, both of which failed significantly.
 
• He was not associated with the construction of Jahaz Mahal as his reign focused on other administrative and military reforms.
 
 
 
• **Sultan Alauddin Khilji**__
 __
 
• **Sultan Alauddin Khilji** was a prominent ruler of the **Khilji dynasty**, known for his military conquests and economic reforms.
 
• He introduced the ** to control prices and ensure the welfare of his subjects.
 
• While he was a visionary ruler, he was not connected to the construction of Jahaz Mahal.
 
 
 
• Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**__
 
 
• **Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** was the founder of the **Tughlaq dynasty** and is renowned for building the fortified city of **Tughlaqabad** in Delhi.
 
• His architectural achievements were focused in Delhi and not in Mandu; hence, he is not associated with Jahaz Mahal.

questions.question: Who was the Iranian ruler who attacked the city of Delhi and took away an immense amount of wealth in 1739?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nadir Shah**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nadir Shah** was the Iranian ruler who attacked the city of Delhi in **1739**.
 
• He was known for his military prowess and ambition to expand his empire.
 
• During his invasion of Delhi, he took away an immense amount of wealth, including the famous** Peacock Throne and Koh-i-Noor diamond**.
 
• Nadir Shah's invasion caused significant destruction and loss of life in the city.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nadir Shah** was the founder of the **Afsharid dynasty in Persia** (modern-day Iran).
 
• His reign lasted from 1736 to 1747, during which he expanded his empire to include parts of the Middle East, South Asia, and Central Asia.
 
• Nadir Shah's invasion of India was partly motivated by the need to replenish his treasury, which had been depleted by continuous military campaigns.
 
• His invasion marked a significant event in the history of the Mughal Empire, leading to its further decline.
 
• After his return to Persia, Nadir Shah continued his campaigns until his assassination in 1747.
